sectionTitle: What changed beyond the sales office

primary.headline: Buyers leaning toward new construction in Texas housing market
primary.summary: Spectrum News 1 reports Austin-area buyers are increasingly choosing new construction over resale as builders lean on incentives to move inventory. The median price for newly built homes in Austin Metro was about $411,000 in July, versus $435,000 for all homes listed area-wide; some communities are advertising first-year mortgage rates as low as 3.25% against a prevailing market rate around 6.625%, plus design credits and closing-cost assistance. Austin realtor Justyn LeFebvre is quoted saying resale sellers increasingly have to price "more in line with where the builders are building."
primary.buyerImplication: New construction is currently underpricing the broader resale market in Austin Metro by roughly $24,000 at the median, and builder rate buydowns are widening that effective gap further -- a structural condition, not a one-off promotion, that buyers should factor into a new-vs-resale comparison right now.
primary.buyerAction: Buyers cross-shopping new vs. resale should compare total cost (price minus incentive value, including the buydown's true cost if it's temporary) rather than list price alone, and ask each builder whether an advertised first-year rate is permanent or reverts after year one.
primary.confidence: High confidence -- Spectrum News 1 reporting; re-verified 2026-08-31, the 19th consecutive daily hold after a fresh multi-angle search pass found no fresher qualifying story. Score sits exactly at the 70-point publish floor. Pete flagged for a decision: widen sourcing to paywalled/non-indexed local outlets, or commission original NHD reporting -- three candidates: the Megatel Homes / MegPrime Pay non-conventional-financing finding (13+ runs unclaimed by any outlet), the Stylecraft 4.99% promo's newly discovered geographic-scope problem (its only named communities are Waco/Houston-area, not core Austin), and the Aug 31 deadline cluster spanning ~10 builders, which lapses today.
